newsitem.title: GERMANY: GERMAN OFFICIALS RELIEVED AS FLOODS EBB SLOWLY.
newsitem.headline: GERMAN OFFICIALS RELIEVED AS FLOODS EBB SLOWLY.

text.p: German officials breathed a sigh of relief on Monday after no new breaches were reported overnight in water-logged flood barriers holding back the swollen River Oder.
But authorities also cautioned there was still a danger dikes could still burst under the sheer pressure of holding back the flooded river on Germany's eastern border for several weeks.
"For the first time, the words 'no special incidents' are in this morning's situation report. It's nice to see that," said Matthias Platzeck, environment minister of Brandenburg state.
Officials stressed, however, that the water levels were only receding very slowly, keeping the strain on the dikes.
"We're not out of the woods yet," Platzeck said. "You can't give any guarantees after nearly three weeks of pressure on the dikes."

The most vulnerable part of the region remained the Oderbruch basin, an area 17 km (11 miles) wide and 50 km (30 miles) long. A breach in the dike could still inundate the area, engulfing villages, farms and factories.
Experts estimate the river needs to fall some one and a half metres (five feet) before the dikes can be deemed safe.
"In the last 24 hours, we've recorded a fall of six centimetres (four inches) at the most important Oderbruch measuring point," Platzeck said. "That doesn't mean any great relief for the dikes."

Soldiers and volunteers worked feverishly over the weekend to bolster the dikes on the Oder and repair new fissures in the dike near the village of Hohenwutzen, the focus of rescue activities in the Oderbruch basin.
Helicopters flew tonnes of sand and gravel to three weak spots near Hohenwutzen, Reitwein and Zollbruecke.

Germany has escaped the worst of a month of flooding from torrential rains in east-central Europe that killed more than 100 people in Poland and the Czech Republic. But damage to German homes, businesses and farms has been extensive.
Officials reported the sharpest fall in water levels south of the Oderbruch region.
In Ratzdorf, where the Oder and Neisse rivers converge, water levels had fallen 17 centimetres (10 inches) in the past 24 hours, a spokeswoman for the local interior ministry said.
The floods have dominated German news bulletins over the past few weeks and networks have also broadcast special programmes daily with the latest news from the region.
Members of the public donated more than four million marks via a special gala programme to raise funds for the relief effort on Sunday night.
